system_description.narrative_title: Democratic midterm sweep reshapes markets, policy and risk pricing
system_description.narrative_summary: A decisive Democratic performance in the U.S. midterms (a 'blue wave') is the dominant story driving the news window: election results shifted investor expectations, triggered broad market moves (equities rally, dollar and yields fall) and sector rotations (data‑center/AI stocks down, renewables up, oil lower). That political shock is feeding through into corporate strategy and earnings narratives while geopolitical flashpoints—notably Iran and Middle East risk—remain modifiers that can reverse commodity and risk premia quickly. The system is open: flows of information, capital and policy signals keep feeding back into asset prices, corporate behavior and diplomatic postures.
system_description.scope: Inside the system: U.S. midterm election outcomes (control of Congress), immediate market reactions (equities, bonds, FX, commodities), sector re‑allocations (AI/data centers, energy, healthcare), investor sentiment and positioning, short‑term policy expectations (legislative oversight, regulatory risk, foreign policy posture), and corporate responses (earnings, restructurings, guidance).
system_description.super_system: Global political‑economic system (international financial markets, cross‑border capital flows and geopolitics).
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. monetary and fiscal policy expectations (Fed, Treasury, debt & spending outlook)
Energy & Middle East geopolitics (oil markets, Iran/Strait of Hormuz risk)
Technology infrastructure investment cycle (AI, data centers, chipmakers)
Corporate governance, M&A and earnings cycle

variables.name: Political control balance
variables.description: The relative degree of legislative and political power alignment across competing political blocs as a continuous measure of control.

variables.name: Policy expectation
variables.description: The market's aggregated expectation of future fiscal, regulatory and foreign‑policy directions over the relevant horizon.

variables.name: Investor sentiment
variables.description: The prevailing risk appetite and confidence level among investors as reflected in positioning and flows.

variables.name: Capital flow volumes
variables.description: The rate and magnitude of cross‑market and cross‑border capital movements into and out of asset classes.

variables.name: Asset price levels
variables.description: The aggregate valuation levels across major asset classes (equities, bonds, FX, commodities) measured continuously.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: The intensity of price fluctuations across financial markets, representing short‑term risk and uncertainty.

variables.name: Sector allocation bias
variables.description: The degree to which portfolios are tilted toward or away from particular economic sectors on an aggregate basis.

variables.name: Regulatory risk perception
variables.description: The perceived likelihood and expected severity of regulatory intervention affecting industries and firms.

variables.name: Corporate profitability trend
variables.description: The ongoing rate of change in aggregate corporate earnings and margins across the market.

variables.name: Corporate guidance sentiment
variables.description: The aggregate tone and conservatism of forward guidance and strategic communications from firms.

variables.name: Geopolitical tension level
variables.description: The prevailing level of international geopolitical friction and conflict risk that can influence markets and commodities.

variables.name: Commodity supply risk
variables.description: The probability and expected magnitude of disruptions to critical commodity supply chains and production.

variables.name: Risk premium levels
variables.description: The market price of risk embedded in asset returns, including equity, sovereign and commodity risk premia.

variables.name: Information flow rate
variables.description: The speed and volume at which news, data and signals propagate through markets and among participants.

variables.name: Market liquidity depth
variables.description: The available depth of tradable liquidity across markets, affecting execution costs and volatility impact.

variables.name: Regulatory oversight intensity
variables.description: The level of active legislative and regulatory scrutiny expected to be applied to sectors and firms.

catalysts.title: Democrats assume congressional control and set agenda
catalysts.description: Democratic midterm sweep consolidates political power, shifting legislative priorities, oversight and market expectations over coming months.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Democrats take Congress', 'Democrats projected to win majority control', 'Markets cheer Democratic win'.

catalysts.title: White House panel hearing on Fed nominee Lisa Cook
catalysts.description: Delayed White House panel hearing for Fed candidate Lisa Cook is now scheduled, a focal date for Fed appointment clarity and market reaction.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'White House panel delays hearing on Fed's Lisa Cook to Dec. 14.'

catalysts.title: Immediate market repricing after Democratic sweep
catalysts.description: Markets and investors reprice yields, equities and risk premia as they digest a Democratic sweep and likely policy continuity or gridlock.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Stocks Jump After Democrats Sweep Congress', 'Treasury Yields Down Following Democrats Midterm Win'.

catalysts.title: Post‑midterms shift toward Middle East de‑escalation
catalysts.description: Election outcome reduces perceived likelihood of US escalation, prompting market hopes for a Middle East solution and lower oil risk.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Oil Prices Sink as U.S. Midterms Raise Market Hopes for Middle East Solution', 'Oil rises on Iran war uncertainty' contrasts with post‑vote easing.

catalysts.title: Local and political chill on data‑centre expansion
catalysts.description: Voter pushback and political attention slow data‑centre projects, pressuring valuations and tilting sector allocations away from hyperscale builds.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI data center stocks slide', 'Voters have put a helpful chill on the US data centre boom'.

catalysts.title: Oil supply normalization from Middle East disruption
catalysts.description: Producers and traders report recovering supplies, which can depress oil prices and lower commodity supply risk in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'JPMorgan, HSBC say oil supplies are recovering from Middle East disruption' and falling oil prices.

catalysts.title: FDA decision on Mineralys' lorundrostat
catalysts.description: Pending FDA decision on lorundrostat will move the biotech's stock and influence near‑term pharma sector sentiment.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Mineralys earnings on deck as FDA decision on lorundrostat looms.'

catalysts.title: China expands overseas mining stakes
catalysts.description: China's overseas mining expansion tightens its grip on critical minerals, changing supply dynamics and strategic risk for markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China expands overseas mining stakes, tightening grip on critical minerals.'

catalysts.title: Continued North Korean weapons launches
catalysts.description: Repeated missile and weapons tests raise short‑term geopolitical risk and market jitters in the region.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'North Korea fires multiple missiles', 'North Korea says it tested air‑defence missile'.

catalysts.title: CVS separation of pharmacy and insurance businesses
catalysts.description: CVS's announced breakup into separate pharmacy and insurance companies will be a multi‑quarter process affecting valuations and sector positioning.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'CVS to break up $117 billion business', 'CVS Health to break up $102bn healthcare empire.'

catalysts.title: Earnings and guidance from AI‑exposed firms
catalysts.description: Upcoming earnings and guidance from AI and chip firms (AMD, Arm, Micron, Qualcomm) will materially reprice AI demand expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AMD Beats', 'Arm Holdings Sales Climb', 'Micron and other chip stocks slip', 'Qualcomm Revenue Falls'.
